nodes.title: Noncrossing partitions split into lonely and marriageable singles partitions

nodes.title: Maximal sets of lanes without U-turns are counted by lonely singles partitions

nodes.summary: In the standard road intersection of size $n$, the lane $E_iX_j$ joins the entry $E_i$ to the exit $X_j$, for $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. A set $S$ of lanes is absolute if it is a maximal set of lanes among all lanes and there are no $i \ne j$ such that $S$ contains both U-turns $E_iX_i$ and $E_jX_j$ and replacing these two lanes in $S$ by $E_iX_j$ and $E_jX_i$ gives again a maximal set of lanes among all lanes.
nodes.title: Absolute maximal set of lanes

nodes.summary: A set partition $P$ of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is a marriageable singles partition if it has two distinct singleton blocks $\{i\}$ and $\{j\}$ such that the partition obtained from $P$ by joining them into the block $\{i, j\}$ has no crossing.

nodes.title: Lower bound for the number of marriageable singles partitions

nodes.summary: For every $n \le 1$, the number of marriageable singles partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ is $M_n = 0$: a marriageable singles partition needs two distinct points.
nodes.title: Small values of the marriageable singles count

nodes.summary: For $n \ge 0$, $M_n$ is the number of noncrossing partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that are marriageable singles partitions.
nodes.title: Number of marriageable singles partitions

nodes.summary: Write $E_iX_j$ for the lane from the $i$-th entry to the $j$-th exit. In the standard road intersection of size $2$, in which every lane is allowed, the maximal sets of lanes are exactly $\{E_1X_1, E_2X_2\}$ and $\{E_1X_2, E_2X_1\}$.
nodes.title: Maximal sets of lanes for an intersection of size two

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a set partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $i, j \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. The partition obtained from $P$ by merging the blocks of $i$ and $j$ has a crossing if there are $a < b < c < d$ in $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ such that $a$ and $c$ lie in one of its blocks and $b$ and $d$ lie in a different one of its blocks.
nodes.title: Crossing after merging two blocks

nodes.summary: Let $P$ be a set partition of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ and let $i, j, x, y \in \{0, \dots, n-1\}$. Then $x$ and $y$ lie in the same block after merging the blocks of $i$ and $j$ if either $x$ and $y$ lie in the same block of $P$, or each of $x$ and $y$ lies in the block of $i$ or in the block of $j$. For singleton blocks $\{i\}$ and $\{j\}$ this joins them into the block $\{i, j\}$.
nodes.title: Same block after merging two blocks

nodes.title: Counting noncrossing partitions with no or one singleton block

nodes.summary: Exactly one noncrossing partition of the empty set has $0$ blocks, $0$ of which are singletons, namely the empty partition; that is, $NC_{0,0,0} = 1$, where $NC_{n,m,k}$ is the number of noncrossing partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ with $m$ blocks of which $k$ are singletons.
nodes.title: Base value of the noncrossing block and singleton count

nodes.summary: For natural numbers $n$, $m$ and $k$, $NC_{n,m,k}$ is the number of noncrossing partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that have exactly $m$ blocks, exactly $k$ of which are singletons.
nodes.title: Noncrossing partitions by number of blocks and of singleton blocks

nodes.summary: Let $M_n$ and $L_n$ be the numbers of noncrossing partitions of $\{0, \dots, n-1\}$ that are marriageable singles partitions and lonely singles partitions, respectively. Then $M_n \to \infty$ and $L_n \to \infty$ as $n \to \infty$.
nodes.title: The marriageable and lonely singles counts tend to infinity

nodes.summary: Extend the binomial coefficient $\binom{a}{b}$ to all integers $a$, $b$ by setting it to $0$ when $a < 0$ or $b < 0$. For all natural numbers $a$ and $b$, this extended binomial coefficient at $a$ and $b$ viewed as integers equals the usual binomial coefficient $\binom{a}{b}$.
nodes.title: The zero-extended binomial coefficient on natural numbers

nodes.summary: Extend the binomial coefficient $\binom{a}{b}$ to all integers $a$, $b$ by setting it to $0$ when $a < 0$ or $b < 0$. Under this convention $\binom{-1}{0} = 0$.
nodes.title: The zero-extended binomial coefficient vanishes at $(-1, 0)$

nodes.summary: For integers $a$ and $b$, the zero-extended binomial coefficient $\binom{a}{b}$ is the usual binomial coefficient of $a$ and $b$ when $a \ge 0$ and $b \ge 0$, and $0$ otherwise.
nodes.title: Zero-extended binomial coefficient
Combinatorics

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
